title: The Rich Young Ruler: Why Good Isn’t Enough
paragraphs: The Rich Young Ruler: Why Good Isn’t Enough
You can look righteous and still walk away from Jesus.

He had money.
He had morality.
He had religion.
He had respect.
Then he ran to Jesus and asked the question that exposes every human heart:

“Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
— Mark 10:17
He thought he needed one more achievement.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Jesus did not expose his wealth first.
He exposed his false goodness.

“No one is good except God alone.”
— Mark 10:18
Read that again.

The young ruler wanted eternal life without surrender.
He wanted salvation as an addition, not a death sentence to his idols.

Jesus named the commandments.
The man said, “Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth.”
You knew.

You knew what it feels like to obey publicly while hiding privately.
You knew what it feels like to say, “I’m a good person,” while avoiding the one thing God keeps touching.
God saw it.
Then Jesus looked at him and loved him.

Not condemned him.
Not mocked him.
Loved him.

“You lack one thing: go, sell all that you have and give to the poor… and come, follow me.”
— Mark 10:21
One thing.

Not because money is evil.
Because money was his master.
Spiritual diagnosis: his hands were full of possessions, so they could not receive Christ.

He wanted eternal life.
But he loved his life too much to lose it.

“Disheartened by the saying, he went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.”
— Mark 10:22
That is the tragedy.

He came running.
He left grieving.
Good wasn’t enough because goodness cannot save you.

“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23

Your morality cannot erase your sin.
Your discipline cannot resurrect your soul.
Your reputation cannot justify you before a holy God.
Only Jesus can.

“By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.”
— Ephesians 2:8–9
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.

The Gospel is not “try harder.”
The Gospel is this:

You sinned.
Christ died.
He rose.
Repent and believe.

“The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
— Luke 19:10

So the question is not, “Am I good?”
The question is, “Have I surrendered?”
Because Jesus does not want to be added to your life.
He is Lord.
